subject: Food Science
title: Microbial Metabolism
description: A short lesson to help you apply Microbial Metabolism.

hook.text: A microbe eating sugar can produce alcohol, acid, or gas depending on its species. Same food, different waste products.

buildup.text: Microbes break down food molecules for energy. Their metabolic byproducts determine what happens to food.

discovery.text: Yeast converts sugar to ethanol and CO₂. That's fermentation—the chemistry behind every beer and bread loaf.

twist.text: Lactic acid bacteria convert sugar to acid instead of alcohol. That acid preserves food and creates tangy flavor.

climax.text: Some bacteria produce hydrogen sulfide—rotten egg smell. Others produce diacetyl—the buttery aroma in fresh popcorn.

punchline.text: What microbes excrete decides if food is delicious or disgusting.

quiz.question: What does yeast produce when it ferments sugar?
